sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in St. Clair County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Five county offices split the work. The Assessor estimates each parcel's value, the Board of Review hears disputes, the County Clerk works out the rate, the Treasurer mails and collects the bill, and the Clerk also runs the annual tax sale. A homeowner who needs help often has to call two of them.

The county lies directly east of St. Louis in the Metro East area, and Belleville is both the seat of government and the biggest city. Its 674 square miles (658 of them land) take in East St. Louis, O'Fallon, Fairview Heights, Mascoutah, Lebanon, Cahokia Heights, Madison and parts of Collinsville and Columbia. I-55, I-64, I-70 and I-255 cross it, 11 MetroLink stations serve it, and Scott Air Force Base lies within it. French settlers founded Cahokia in 1697, and a proclamation in 1790 created the county, the first one in what became Illinois.

If you plan to sell, collect three things early: the Treasurer's payment record for your parcel, the Assessor's property record card and a clear idea of how the year's tax will be divided at closing.

sections.h2: How do St. Clair County housing numbers compare inside the county?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 250,708 residents for July 1, 2025, compared with 257,400 counted in 2020. A typical owned home is valued at $180,300 and typical rent is $1,090, and 68.4% of homes have an owner living in them. Household income at the midpoint is $73,854, and 12.7% of residents are below the poverty line (QuickFacts, 2020-2024).

Owning costs $1,645 a month at the midpoint for mortgage holders and $645 for owners with no loan. The county has 100,846 households averaging 2.47 people. Treat these as county-wide markers and look at actual sales near your own address.

sections.h2: When do St. Clair County property tax installments fall due?
sections.html:
Each year's tax is billed in the following year and paid in two installments. The Treasurer's schedule for 2025 taxes payable in 2026 appears below, with the office noting that every date was tentative. Those dates have passed, so ask the Treasurer for the schedule covering your next bill.

St. Clair County Treasurer schedule, 2025 taxes payable in 2026
StepDate
First installment dueJuly 1, 2026
Second installment dueSeptember 1, 2026
Final payment before the saleOctober 30, 2026
Annual tax saleNovember 2, 2026

Source: St. Clair County Treasurer, Collection Dates. The Treasurer also set a September 18 deadline to avoid newspaper publication. Electronic payment stops at 3 p.m. on that day and on the final payment day, and a postmark earns no grace.

sections.h2: What does a late or unpaid bill cost in St. Clair County?
sections.html:
Illinois adds a penalty of 1.5% of the unpaid balance for each month an installment is late, and it steps up by another 1.5% every thirty days. Each payment coupon prints the total with penalty. Only the Treasurer's office accepts partial payments, since collector banks refuse them.

A lien for unpaid tax can be sold. On a principal dwelling with six or fewer apartment units the owner may redeem for two and one-half years, and on other property for two years. Redemption means paying the tax along with penalties and interest, and an owner who never redeems can lose the property. Anyone selling a house with unpaid tax should plan to clear it at closing.

  • An escrow account does not shift responsibility. The Treasurer says the owner answers for the bill whatever the bank or servicer arranged.
  • The Treasurer does not report to credit bureaus, so a late bill does not touch your score.
  • Pay by mail, in person, at listed collector banks through the second due date, or online. Cards cost 2.5% with a $2.00 minimum.

sections.h2: How can an owner contest a St. Clair County assessment?
sections.html:
Begin with your bill and the property record card from the Assessor. Check that every exemption you qualify for shows up and that the card's facts are right. The Assessor measures a home's outside perimeter for square footage, so your interior measurement will be smaller. Assessed value equals one-third of estimated market value, and the estimate rests on recent sales of similar homes.

If an informal talk with the Assessor settles nothing, file with the elected three-member Board of Review at 10 Public Square, Belleville, IL 62220. You have 30 days from the point the Assessor revises assessments. Useful evidence includes a photo of your house, photos and property record cards for three comparable homes, or a recent appraisal, sales contract, settlement statement or deed. Papers must be at the Board's office five days or more before the hearing, or the assessment stands. After that, the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board is the next level.

A separate route, the Tax Objection Complaint, goes through the Circuit Clerk. It mostly serves rate disputes and is due within 75 days after the second installment date.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and deferrals can reduce a St. Clair County bill?
sections.html:
Homeowners can claim the general homestead exemption for an owner-occupied residence, and veterans, returning veterans and people with disabilities have separate ones. The county posts three senior programs on its Treasurer page.

  • Senior homestead exemption: takes $5,000 off the assessed value of a home owned and lived in by someone 65 or older.
  • Senior assessment freeze: locks the assessed value for qualifying owners. The Assessor, at 618-825-2704, sends the application.
  • Senior tax deferral: the state pays the tax and records a lien, then recovers it with 6% annual interest when the home is sold or transferred. Plan for repayment at closing if the owner used it. The Treasurer, at 618-825-2440, supplies the forms.

The Treasurer also runs a monthly payment plan for current-tax homeowners who hold the homeowner occupied exemption. Sign-up begins in August and payments start in September, with no change to the due dates.

sections.h2: How is the tax split when a St. Clair County house sells?
sections.html:
Illinois collects property tax after the year it covers, so a seller owes for the months of ownership and the closing statement credits the buyer for that share. The Assessor's office points owners to their closing papers for the proportionate credit.

Get the Treasurer's record for the parcel before signing anything, and learn whether the latest bill is paid, open or sold. Inherited, rented and long-empty houses are the ones most likely to carry a delinquency. Tax sale questions go to the County Clerk at 618-277-6600, and exemption questions go to the Board of Review at 618-825-2489.

Keep the parcel number, the most recent bill and proof of your exemptions in one folder. A cash purchaser will ask for the same paperwork as any other buyer.

faqs.q: How many installments does St. Clair County collect, and when?
faqs.a: Two per year. For 2025 taxes payable in 2026 the Treasurer listed July 1 and September 1, all marked tentative. Call the Treasurer's office for the dates on your next bill.

faqs.q: How fast does a late St. Clair County bill grow?
faqs.a: By 1.5% of the unpaid balance each month, a penalty set by the State of Illinois. Your payment coupon shows the figure with penalty included.

faqs.q: When must I file a St. Clair County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: Within 30 days of the Assessor revising assessments, with the Board of Review. A rate challenge through the Circuit Clerk has its own limit of 75 days after the second installment date.

faqs.q: Can a St. Clair County owner get the house back after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, by redeeming. A principal dwelling with six or fewer apartments has two and one-half years, other property two years, and redemption costs the tax plus penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Which St. Clair County office should a senior call for tax relief?
faqs.a: The Treasurer at 618-825-2440 for deferral forms, the Assessor at 618-825-2704 for the assessment freeze, and the Board of Review at 618-825-2489 if the $5,000 senior homestead exemption is missing from your bill.
